findings.issue_text: [BUG] The added gate isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns false whenever user is null, so UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() and challenge(context,error,field) now call webAuthnAuth.fillContextForm() only for an already-identified user — the exact inverse of the user==null condition they replaced — and the passkey conditional-UI form attributes (WebAuthnConstants.ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, challenge, rp, timeouts) are never set on the initial username+password page where context.getUser() is null. On a fresh visit to any realm whose browser flow uses the combined username/password form, the rendered login page has no <form id='webauth'> and the username input's autocomplete is "username" instead of "username webauthn", so passkey conditional mediation silently disappears from the first login page (and from invalid-username retry pages rendered through challenge(context,error,field)) — a regression of the shipped passkeys feature. The diff's own tests prove the contradiction: webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication and webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest call oauth.openLoginForm() right after logout() with no user identified, then assert loginPage.getUsernameAutocomplete() is "username webauthn" (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java, lines ~189 and ~350 of the new file content) and that driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")) is not null — the first assertion fails on the autocomplete value and the second throws NoSuchElementException, so these new tests can never pass against this implementation; the fix is to not require user != null (UsernameForm's no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() shows the correct user-agnostic gate, and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() already distinguishes the user-identified case internally).

[BUG] The rewrite of challenge(context, error, field) from `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` (which returns false when user is null, per the `user != null` clause added at lines 160-162) inverts the gate and removes conditional-UI setup from error pages rendered for unidentified users. On a passkeys-enabled realm using the combined username/password execution, a user who submits an unknown username (nullUserHandler -> challenge(error,field) with user == null) gets an error page with no webauthn form and no conditional mediation, so the passkey option that pre-PR code armed on exactly that page (the natural remedy when you cannot remember your username) vanishes mid-flow and the user must restart the login; no test in the diff asserts webauthn presence on an unidentified-user error page (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey checks only the error text).

[ADVISORY] The new AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) call on the passkey-failure re-render path (createErrorResponse) is exercised by no test in the diff — every re-auth test uses successful passkey attempts or password failures, none triggers a failed passkey assertion during re-authentication. A regression on this changed path ships green: if the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note is not actually set when the failure arrives via the webauthn form action rather than a password submit, the re-auth error page renders a visible username field and a registration link (or loses the re-armed conditional UI), and nothing in CI notices.

[ADVISORY] Suppressing the re-auth skip whenever passkeys are enabled means every prompt=login re-auth on the default flow renders the username form even for users who own no passkey credential, yet PasskeysUsernameFormTest's only re-auth test uses a discoverable key whose conditional mediation auto-completes past the rendered page, so nothing asserts what the re-auth username page actually shows. Passkey-less users in passkeys-enabled realms gain a spurious username re-entry step before the password form on every re-auth (pre-PR they skipped straight to the password form), and whether that page hides/prefills the username or even lets the already-identified user submit a different username and switch re-auth identity is left unverified — a broken or identity-switchable re-auth username form would pass CI.

[ADVISORY] Hard-coding shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to false removes fillContextForm's empty-authenticators early return for identified users, so re-auth/identified pages now arm the passkey option from realm policy alone, without checking that the user owns a credential conditional mediation can actually surface (discoverable passkey). Identified users whose webauthn credentials are absent or non-discoverable (e.g. the org test's own userwebauthn, whose non-discoverable key cannot be offered by a conditional request with empty allowCredentials) are shown a passkey control that can never complete; clicking it drops them into the equally-untested createErrorResponse loop — reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey verifies only the policy-disabled variant of this page, never the policy-enabled/passkey-less-user one.

[ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError re-implements the `Boolean.parseBoolean(getAuthNote(USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH))` check that already exists as AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth, and the constant was promoted from protected to public solely to feed this second copy. The re-auth flag now has two independent parsers; a future change to the note's writer or semantics applied in the abstract-class method but not this util silently diverges badPasswordHandler's error-form rendering from the user-retention logic reading the same note, and every reviewer must diff two implementations to confirm today's equivalence.

[ADVISORY] The webauth-form absence check asserts via driver.findElement inside catch (Exception), so any driver failure other than a present-element AssertionError (stale element, session timeout, crashed browser) is swallowed and the block passes as 'no webauthn button'. The absence guarantee for the initial login page is unenforced — an intermittent WebDriverException or a template regression that breaks the page turns this test green instead of red; the same diff deletes the precise Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) idiom (PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) that should have been reused here.

[ADVISORY] The second webauth-form absence check (re-auth page after prompt=login) repeats the catch (Exception) swallow-all pattern, so any non-NoSuchElementException WebDriver failure passes as 'passkeys not offered during re-auth'. The core regression this PR fixes — passkeys disappearing from the re-auth page — is guarded by a check that also passes when the driver or page is broken, so a future re-introduction of the bug under a broken-page condition is not caught; assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) is the correct idiom.

[BUG] Moving the webauthn setup out of the GET branch while gating it on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) (which requires user != null) deletes the only code in this diff that set up conditional-passkeys data for the anonymous (user == null) login render, and no code in the diff replaces it. A first-time visitor to the username/password page of a passkeys-enabled realm gets no webAuthnData on the initial GET (authenticate's gate is user != null and the challenge(error, field) gate is also user != null), so the 'username webauthn' autocomplete and the webauthn form vanish from initial login — exactly what the diff's own unchanged assertions in restructured passwordLoginWithExternalKey (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, getUsernameAutocomplete()=="username webauthn" plus //form[@id='webauth'] present) require; this removal is not traceable to the re-authentication requirement.

[BUG] The challenge(context, error, field) condition is flipped from "user == null && passkeys enabled" to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) (user != null), so the conditional-UI setup for anonymous error renders is removed rather than extended. badPasswordHandler (this diff, line ~222) routes failed-login error renders through this override; a user who submits an unknown/empty username at initial login now gets the re-rendered page without webAuthnData, so the passkey option that pre-diff survived a username typo (the explicit purpose of the old "user is not already selected" branch) disappears from the error page, and the same anonymous error paths lose the setup with no in-diff replacement.

[BUG] Overriding shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to return false unconditionally bypasses the authenticators.isEmpty() early-return in WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm (line ~101), so webAuthnData is emitted for every identified-user page render regardless of whether the user owns any usable passkey. Every re-authentication and post-username page in a passkeys-enabled realm now renders the webauthn 'Authenticate' action for users it cannot serve: password-only users get a dead passkey button on every re-auth, and users whose only credential is non-discoverable (the organization test's own userwebauthn) get an action whose discoverable-credentials request can never match them — the flipped assertion in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest line ~200 institutionalizes showing this unusable UI; the diff's test for it (reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey) sidesteps the case by disabling the realm policy instead of testing a passkey-less user with the policy on.

[ADVISORY] The PR changes first-time organization-login behavior (passkey UI now rendered on the post-username password page) — not a re-authentication scenario — and encodes it by inverting a pre-existing assertion inside an existing password-login test rather than adding scoped coverage. Operators of organization realms get a user-visible change to the initial login flow (passkey button appearing mid-login, including the unusable-button case for non-discoverable-key users) shipped inside a PR titled as a re-authentication fix; if the new first-login behavior regresses, no dedicated test isolates it, since this test proceeds straight to password login without exercising the newly required webauthn form.

[ADVISORY] The new webauthn-absence checks use a try { assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) {} antipattern (repeated again at ~lines 288-292) instead of the Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) pattern this same PR keeps using in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest. catch (Exception) swallows every non-assertion driver failure (stale element, timeout, wrong page) as 'expected', so the absence check passes vacuously on a broken page and future regressions of webauthn-suppression go undetected; the fail() line is dead code when the element is present because assertThat throws AssertionError (an Error, not caught by catch (Exception)) before it, misleading the next reader about what the test actually verifies.

[ADVISORY] reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey is named and commented for 'user does not have passkey' but actually tests realm-policy-disabled (setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)), leaving the invariant its name promises — passkeys enabled in policy while the user has no passkey credential — completely uncovered by this diff. The exact regression the re-auth fix can introduce (webauthn UI shown to a passkey-less user when the policy is on, per the bypassed empty-credentials guard) ships unverified; a future reader trusting the test name believes per-user gating is covered when only the policy gate is, so a regression in per-user suppression breaks no test.

[ADVISORY] The new skip condition gates on the realm passkeys policy (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) rather than on the re-authenticating user actually owning a passkey, so every re-authenticating user loses the skip when the policy is on. In flows built on the Username Form execution, password-only users in a passkeys-enabled realm gain an extra interactive page on every re-authentication (pre-diff they skipped straight to the password step) whose conditional UI offers them nothing; the cost of enabling passkeys realm-wide is imposed on users who cannot use them, and the gate cannot distinguish them.

[ADVISORY] webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication is a near-verbatim ~55-line copy of the identically named test added in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest, and the five-line passwordless-policy setup block is repeated four times across the new tests while setPasswordlessPolicyForExternalKey was extracted in only one file. The next change to the passkeys policy matrix (e.g., a new required WebAuthn policy knob) must be synchronized across 6+ scattered blocks in three files with no single source of truth — drift has already started inside this diff (one file extracted the helper, the twin files kept inline copies), so the copies will diverge and one realm's tests will silently test a different policy than the others.

[ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError introduces a second, independent parser of the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note in a different package (enabled by making the constant public) while the pre-existing isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth reader in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator — still used by the user-clearing logic the constant's own comment describes — keeps its own copy instead of delegating. The re-auth note contract is now interpreted in two packages with two hand-maintained parsers; a future change to the note's semantics (e.g., when it is set during the GET branch) must be applied in both places, and missing one yields divergent re-auth behavior between the password-error form setup and the user-clearing path — the old reader should delegate to the new util so only one interpreter exists.

[BUG] The error-render guard in challenge(context, error, field) is inverted from `context.getUser() == null` (fill WebAuthn data for unidentified users) to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` (which requires user != null), so after this diff no code path in UsernamePasswordForm sets up conditional passkey data on unidentified-user error pages. In a passkeys-enabled realm using the combined username+password form, a user who mistypes their username or password on initial login (context user deliberately unbound, per the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH clearing semantics) gets an error re-render with no webauthn form and no conditional-UI challenge data — exactly the case the removed `context.getUser() == null` branch used to fill — so the passkey option that existed before the failed attempt disappears and the user must reload the login page from scratch to use a passkey; the PR's own re-auth test insists passkeys must survive a failed password attempt, but no test asserts the webauthn element on an initial-login error page, so this mirror-image regression ships silently.

[ADVISORY] The re-authentication skip is now gated on the realm-wide passkeys policy (`!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`) instead of on whether the already-known user holds any WebAuthn credential, even though `context.getUser()` is non-null exactly at this branch and could be checked. Every re-authentication (prompt=login, max_age step-up, required-action re-verify, admin-console verify) in a passkeys-enabled realm with the default browser flow now stops at a username form for ALL users, including password-only users who cannot use a passkey at all; the diff adds no pre-fill/hide handling for the bound user on this newly reachable render, so such users must stop at and submit a username form where the pre-change flow took them straight to the password step, and this realistic configuration (policy on, user has no passkey) is exercised by no test in the diff.

[ADVISORY] Removing the skip re-opens the username-submission path during re-authentication without adding any check that the submitted username matches the user already bound to the re-authentication session — the pre-change `context.success()` skip was the structural invariant that this form never appears once a user is bound, and nothing replaces it. A step-up re-authentication initiated to re-verify user A (required actions, admin-console verification) now presents a username input that accepts user B's name, and nothing in this diff prevents the flow from continuing under B: UsernameForm.action was written for the user-unbound case and is not made to enforce the bound identity, so the identity being re-verified is decided by fresh form input rather than by the session that requested the step-up.

[ADVISORY] The new reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test advertises coverage of 're-authentication with password when passkeys feature enabled ... user does not have passkey', but it disables the realm passkeys policy entirely (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`), so it exercises the policy gate rather than the user-credential scenario its name and comment claim. The genuinely new and untested path — policy ON, user has no WebAuthn credential, re-authenticating, where the combined form now renders a passkey button that cannot succeed and the separate username form forces username re-entry — can regress while CI reports the without-passkey case as covered; a maintainer reading the test name believes the user-agnostic gating is verified when only the policy-off branch is.

[ADVISORY] The conditional-passkeys decision is now spread across a family of same-named predicates with hand-maintained complementary user-gates — isPasskeysEnabled() (policy only), UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() (policy only), UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) (policy AND user != null, with the user requirement buried in the last conjunct), and shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) (user != null in the base, hard false in the conditional subclass) — with the fillContextForm call itself distributed across render paths each carrying its own user condition. Gate drift is the exact defect class this PR fixes, and this same diff introduces a new instance (the challenge(error) inversion): the next editor who 'unifies' the two same-named isConditionalPasskeysEnabled methods, or adjusts one gate without its complement, silently disables passkey setup on either initial login or re-authentication with no compile error; a single rule — fill whenever passkeys are enabled and let shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators own user-dependence — would delete the per-site user checks and the drift surface.

[ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError re-implements the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH check inline (Boolean.parseBoolean of the raw auth note) instead of reusing AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth, widening the constant to public and making the authenticators.util package depend on the authenticators.browser package (static import) while browser authenticators call back into the util. The re-auth-detection predicate now lives in two places in two packages: a future change to when the note is written, or to what isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth checks, updates one reader and silently skips the other, so the password-error path and the WebAuthn-error path render the re-authentication form state inconsistently (username hidden on one error page, visible on the other); a single shared static predicate would delete the duplicated reading logic and the new package cycle.

[BUG] challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext, String, String) inverts its passkey-setup gate from context.getUser() == null to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires a non-null user, deleting the deliberate unidentified-user setup the old code documented ('setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected') from the error-render path. In a passkeys-enabled realm, a user who submits an unknown username on the combined username+password form gets the error page rendered with no webauthn conditional-UI data: the passkey button and the 'username webauthn' autofill that pre-PR re-setup delivered vanish after one failed attempt and only return on a full page reload. This silently regresses the first-login passkeys flow that a PR titled 'Fixing Re-authentication with passkeys' never claimed to touch, and no test in the diff asserts webauthn presence on that error page (passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey checks only the error text).

[ADVISORY] The PR silently reverses an accepted first-login behavior: the username+password page shown to an already-identified user changes from 'passkeys disabled' (previously asserted via NoSuchElementException with an explicit explanatory comment) to 'Passkeys still enabled', expanding the objective from re-authentication to every identity-first/organization login with no recorded acceptance of that product change. All identity-first and organization flows in passkeys-enabled realms now render passkey UI on the identified-user password page for every user; operators upgrading get a changed login UX whose only acceptance record is a rewritten test comment, and the test that previously testified to the original 'passkeys disabled' decision no longer exists to document why that decision was made.

[BUG] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators returns false unconditionally, so identified-user pages build the passkey request with isUserIdentified=false (policy-based, no allowCredentials) and can never present the user's registered authenticators, leaving users whose only WebAuthn credential is non-discoverable with a passkey button that cannot invoke their key. A user holding only a non-discoverable security key — precisely the scenario of the flipped passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey assertion, which now demands the webauth form be present — clicks 'Authenticate' and the browser offers no matching passkey, because a discoverable-only request cannot select non-discoverable credentials; the result is a dead-end button where pre-PR correctly rendered nothing, and the flipped test verifies element presence, not function, so the defect ships green.

[ADVISORY] The re-auth skip is now keyed on the realm-level isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() alone, so in passkeys-enabled realms every identified user — including users with no WebAuthn credential at all — loses the direct skip to the next execution and must traverse the username page on every re-authentication (prompt=login). Password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms pay an extra page interaction on every step-up/re-auth — a mainstream-population change unrelated to the passkey holders the fix targets — and the passkeys-enabled + user-without-passkey re-auth combination is exercised by no test in the diff (the new tests cover has-passkey and passkeys-disabled only), so a rendering regression in UsernameForm's identified-user path would break step-up login for the majority population with zero test signal.

[ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError re-implements the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth-note check that already exists as AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth, creating two hand-maintained copies of the re-auth detection logic. The next change to the re-auth marker (note key, value format, or where it is stored) must be replicated in both the util and the protected method; miss one and the password error path and the passkey error path disagree about whether a form is a re-authentication form, breaking the username-hidden/registration-disabled rendering for exactly one of the two flows.

[ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) means 'passkeys enabled AND user identified' while the same-named no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() in the parent UsernameForm means only 'passkeys enabled', and the challenge() call site in this diff used the user-aware overload where only the feature check was meant. The next maintainer who calls the identically-named helper intending 'is the passkeys feature on' silently acquires a user != null gate — the exact conflation that produced this diff's error-page condition inversion — and the accompanying comment ('setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled' over a user-gated call) tells them nothing about the trap.

[ADVISORY] The new AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call in createErrorResponse — the branch that keeps a failed passkey's error page in re-authentication mode — is executed by no test in the diff, and neither call site's observable effect (USERNAME_HIDDEN / REGISTRATION_DISABLED form attributes) is asserted anywhere. A regression in the re-auth passkey error path — e.g. the auth note not surviving to createErrorResponse, or fillContextForm clobbering the attributes — ships silently; a user mid-step-up who fails a passkey gets a full login form with an editable username field and a registration link instead of the constrained re-authentication form, with no CI signal to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The re-authentication tests added by this diff (webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey here, plus webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication in PasskeysUsernameFormTest and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) complete re-authentication only with the re-auth user's own passkey, so the state this diff newly enables — WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.action running with a pre-set context.getUser() while the conditional-UI discoverable credential can resolve to a different account — has no test asserting that a cross-user passkey is rejected. Conditional mediation surfaces every discoverable passkey the browser holds for the RP, so on a shared machine/profile the re-auth page offers other accounts' passkeys as one-gesture completions of a step-up; a missing or regressed user-binding check in the newly-reachable action() path would let one account's passkey satisfy another account's re-authentication and reach release with every re-auth test green, since all new tests exercise only the happy path.

[ADVISORY] The unconditional shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() == false override forces fillContextForm down the unidentified/discoverable branch even during re-authentication, when context.getUser() is already set, so the re-auth passkey request is issued without the re-auth user's credential allow-list. During a step-up re-authentication the browser's conditional mediation therefore offers every discoverable passkey registered for the RP on that browser — including other accounts' passkeys — and rejection of a foreign credential rests entirely on the server-side user binding in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.action rather than being excluded from the request; users on shared machines see other accounts offered mid-step-up, and any gap in that binding check turns a UI choice into an authentication bypass.

[ADVISORY] UsernameForm now falls through to render the anonymous username-entry form during re-authentication whenever conditional passkeys are enabled (previously the execution skipped straight to success), while the same diff's AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError enforces the opposite policy for the identical 'user already set' state by hiding the username field (USERNAME_HIDDEN) on re-auth password-error pages. A re-authenticating user in a passkeys-enabled realm is handed a blank, freely editable username field at the front of a step-up flow whose later pages deliberately pin the user, so the same-user re-auth invariant is enforced on one new path introduced by this diff and unenforced on the other; a maintainer who later hardens one path (as this diff itself does for the password page) leaves the other silently divergent, and the security of step-up now leans on the untested action()-side handling of a resubmitted username against a pre-set user.

[BUG] The initial-page webauthn-absence check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey wraps assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath('//form[@id=webauth']')), nullValue()) in try/catch(Exception), so the only passing path is an exception being swallowed: findElement never returns null so the assertThat can never succeed, and the fail('Not expected to have webauthn button') line is unreachable in both branches. Any exception other than NoSuchElementException - a mistyped XPath throwing InvalidSelectorException, a WebDriver timeout, a stale-page error - is caught and silently counted as 'no webauthn button', so the assertion passes while the check itself is broken; the idiom this same PR removed (Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) fails loudly on exactly those conditions.

[BUG] The re-authentication-page webauthn-absence check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey repeats the same catch(Exception)-around-nullValue() pattern, converting every possible lookup failure into a silent pass. During the prompt=login re-authentication step - the core scenario this PR exists to test - a driver or selector failure (InvalidSelectorException, timeout, session error) is reported as 'webauthn correctly absent', so the assertion that passkeys are hidden for a user without a passkey can pass without the page ever having been checked.

[ADVISORY] The new createErrorResponse call to AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError - added precisely to keep the re-authentication form state (hidden username, disabled registration) when a conditional-UI passkey fails during re-authentication - is never executed by any test in this diff. Checked all three changed test files (PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java, PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java): every virtual-authenticator passkey operation succeeds and the only failures exercised are password failures routed through badPasswordHandler, so a regression in the failed-passkey-during-re-auth path (wrong form rendered, or an exception in the new call aborting fillContextForm) ships with a fully green suite; any pre-existing passkey-failure tests outside this diff run with the authNote unset and take the no-op branch, so they cannot detect it either.

[ADVISORY] The new shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators override (always false, suppressing the identified-user authenticator rendering during conditional-UI login) is not pinned by any assertion in the diff's tests, which assert only the presence of the //form[@id='webauth'] element that fillContextForm emits in both the list-shown and list-suppressed variants. Reverting the override to the inherited 'user != null' behavior leaves every test in this diff green (PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey's notNullValue assertion passes either way) while re-authentication and identified-user pages switch to identified-user/2FA-style rendering - the deliberate decision documented in the new comment has no test that fails when it is broken.

[ADVISORY] The new skip-condition (!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) that makes UsernameForm render during re-authentication when passkeys are enabled has no assertion distinguishing it from the old skip behavior - webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication in PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java (and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java) goes from prompt=login directly to appPage.assertCurrent() with no loginPage.assertCurrent() or page-content check. Reverting the condition restores the silent context.success() skip during re-auth and the tests stay green, because the following password-form execution (which this diff's UsernamePasswordForm change fills with webauthn data whenever user != null) also carries the conditional UI and auto-logs-in the discoverable key - so the page-presentation behavior this diff deliberately changed is unverified and can silently regress; contrast PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, whose re-auth tests do assert the presented page ('Please re-authenticate to continue' plus webauthn form presence).

[BUG] The flipped gate in challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext, String, String) removes the WebAuthn conditional-UI setup from error pages rendered while no user is selected, so the re-rendered page after a failed initial username/password attempt no longer includes the passkey (webauth) form that this same site provided before the change and that the initial login page still shows. A user in a passkeys-enabled realm whose browser flow uses the combined username+password form and who mistypes their username (invalidUser path, context.getUser()==null) or password gets a re-rendered error page with no passkey sign-in option, silently losing the passkey alternative exactly on the failure path (pre-PR this site filled the webauthn data when user==null); no test asserts the webauth form on this error page, so the regression ships unnoticed and users must reload the login to get the passkey autofill back.

[BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate now renders an interactive username form whenever context.getUser() is already set and the realm-level passkeys policy is enabled, regardless of which authentication flow is executing, so every flow that relied on the user!=null auto-skip — notably the reset-credentials flow's 'Choose user' execution when the user is already identified — inserts a mandatory username step instead of auto-advancing. Every user of a passkeys-enabled realm who enters their username on the login page and then clicks 'Forgot password?' is asked to type the username again on the reset-credentials 'choose user' page (a typo there invalidUser's them out of the reset entirely), even for users who have no passkey credential, because the gate checks only the realm policy; the gate cannot distinguish the browser re-authentication flow the PR intends from credential-reset or other flows reusing auth-username-form with a known user.

[ADVISORY] The newly extracted setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError helper is applied only at badPasswordHandler and the conditional-UI createErrorResponse, while the other challenge renders reachable during re-authentication (brute-force lockout via bruteForceDelayedChallenge, disabled-user) still build their pages without calling it. A re-authenticating user who trips brute-force protection gets an error page with a visible, editable username input and an enabled registration link, while the adjacent wrong-password page correctly hides both; nothing signals to the next contributor adding an error path that the helper must be invoked per call site, so the re-auth page-shape desync grows with each new error path.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: [ADVISORY] The re-auth skip is now keyed on the realm-level isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() alone, so in passkeys-enabled realms every identified user — including users with no WebAuthn credential at all — loses the direct skip to the next execution and must traverse the username page on every re-authentication (prompt=login). Password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms pay an extra page interaction on every step-up/re-auth — a mainstream-population change unrelated to the passkey holders the fix targets — and the passkeys-enabled + user-without-passkey re-auth combination is exercised by no test in the diff (the new tests cover has-passkey and passkeys-disabled only), so a rendering regression in UsernameForm's identified-user path would break step-up login for the majority population with zero test signal.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The golden issue is that UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without the required UserModel, causing the logic to be evaluated only at the realm level rather than per-user. The candidate report describes exactly that behavioral consequence: re-auth skip is keyed on realm-level isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() alone, affecting users without WebAuthn credentials. This aligns with the same underlying bug (missing user parameter leading to realm-only gating).

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: [BUG] The added gate isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns false whenever user is null, so UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() and challenge(context,error,field) now call webAuthnAuth.fillContextForm() only for an already-identified user — the exact inverse of the user==null condition they replaced — and the passkey conditional-UI form attributes (WebAuthnConstants.ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, challenge, rp, timeouts) are never set on the initial username+password page where context.getUser() is null. On a fresh visit to any realm whose browser flow uses the combined username/password form, the rendered login page has no <form id='webauth'> and the username input's autocomplete is "username" instead of "username webauthn", so passkey conditional mediation silently disappears from the first login page (and from invalid-username retry pages rendered through challenge(context,error,field)) — a regression of the shipped passkeys feature. The diff's own tests prove the contradiction: webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication and webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest call oauth.openLoginForm() right after logout() with no user identified, then assert loginPage.getUsernameAutocomplete() is "username webauthn" (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java, lines ~189 and ~350 of the new file content) and that driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")) is not null — the first assertion fails on the autocomplete value and the second throws NoSuchElementException, so these new tests can never pass against this implementation; the fix is to not require user != null (UsernameForm's no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() shows the correct user-agnostic gate, and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() already distinguishes the user-identified case internally).
